s1.syndrome_frame: Jaw pain and tooth mobility with radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion
salient_findings: Tender percussion of the right mandibular second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Buccolingual expansion with cortical thinning on cone beam CT
key_facts: Pain and slight mobility of the mandibular right second premolar and first molar
Slight mobility of the affected teeth
Bony-hard consistency of the buccal and lingual cortices
Lesion extends to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal
Cone beam CT shows buccolingual expansion with cortical thinning

shortlist.label: Odontogenic keratocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Matches radiographic findings of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion

shortlist.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the clinical presentation of jaw pain and tooth mobility, and radiographic evidence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion

shortlist.label: Radicular cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of the radiolucent lesion, although the irregular shape is atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas

shortlist.label: Dentigerous cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Could be a consideration given the location and radiographic appearance of the lesion, although less likely than odontogenic keratocyst or unicystic ameloblastoma

shortlist.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to odontogenic keratocyst, but with potential for more aggressive behavior, and should be considered in the differential diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and cortical thinning, as well as the atypical irregular shape for routine periapical cysts or granulomas, supports the diagnosis of an odontogenic keratocyst, now more commonly referred to as a keratocystic odontogenic tumor, which is known for its aggressive behavior and potential for growth.

rejected.label: Unicystic ameloblastoma
rejected.why: While unicystic ameloblastoma can present as a unilocular radiolucency, the clinical and radiographic features provided do not specifically suggest the characteristic unilocular appearance with scalloped borders typically seen in unicystic ameloblastoma.

rejected.label: Radicular cyst
rejected.why: The irregular shape of the lesion and its extension to the superior border of the inferior alveolar nerve canal are atypical for a radicular cyst, which is usually associated with the apex of a non-vital tooth and has a more rounded shape.

rejected.label: Dentigerous cyst
rejected.why: There is no mention of an unerupted tooth associated with the lesion, which is a key feature of dentigerous cysts, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Keratocystic odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This is essentially the same entity as odontogenic keratocyst, with the term keratocystic odontogenic tumor being the currently preferred nomenclature due to its neoplastic nature, but the provided shortlist includes both terms, and odontogenic keratocyst was chosen as the champion due to its direct match in the provided options.
